    • Global Constraints
    • File Structure
      • Task 1: Fix the campaign regime grouping key to include base timeframe
      • Task 2: Add base timeframe to the ideal-composite section
      • Task 3: Episode timeline type and builder
      • Task 4: Render and serialize the episode timeline

    1. Home

    ARCHIVED 2026-07-11 — DONE. All 8 tasks implemented, gate-green (29/29 tests, modules/core 416 regression). One deferred item split out to docs/mini-plans/20260711_PER_RUN_REPORT_REGIME_ENRICHMENT.md.

    Campaign Ideal Report Redesign Implementation Plan

    For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

    Goal: Fix the campaign regime grouping so a strategy's own base timeframe never mixes with a different one under the same symbol and labeling config, then split the campaign ideal-composite report into one self-contained Markdown+JSON file per (symbol, base_timeframe, labeling_config) group plus a linked index, each carrying a chronological episode timeline of "which regime was active, and which strategy served it" — distinguishing a real data gap (no contributing experiment covers that span) from a covered span the winner simply didn't trade. Also add Symbol / Base TF / Range columns to the plain campaign leaderboard, which today lists every experiment in one flat table with no way to tell which symbol or timeframe a row belongs to.

    Architecture: Part A (regime_reporting.py) groups campaign trials by a 3-tuple key instead of 2, so campaign_report.json never pools two different base timeframes into one regime section; it also resolves symbol/base-timeframe/range for every leaderboard row so the campaign leaderboard itself never mixes symbols invisibly. Part B (campaign_ideal_report.py and its pure-builder modules) reads that corrected campaign_report.json, composes one IdealSectionComposite per group exactly as before, but now also builds a per-routing episode timeline (contiguous regime-bucket runs, each attributed to its winner's real trades and marked covered or not against the group's actual contributing date ranges), and the CLI writes one Markdown+JSON pair per group into a campaign_ideal/ subfolder plus an index.md linking every group ordered by headline net PnL.

    Tech Stack: Python 3.11, Polars, frozen slotted dataclasses, pytest, the rainbow.* editable packages.

    Global Constraints

    • Every touched Python file must pass, with no suppressions (# type: ignore / # noqa / pylint: disable are forbidden — fix the root cause):
    • .venv/bin/ruff check <file>
    • MYPYPATH="$(ls -d modules/*/src | tr '\n' ':')" .venv/bin/mypy --strict <file> (MYPYPATH, not PYTHONPATH — required for this repo's src-layout namespace packages)
    • .venv/bin/pyright <file>
    • .venv/bin/pylint <file> — score ≥ 9.5
    • Run tests with .venv/bin/python -m pytest scripts/experiments/tests/<file> -v (repo root is on sys.path via the registered scripts/experiments/tests pytest path). The IDE/LSP may show reportMissingImports for scripts.* in test files — that is an LSP false positive; the pyright CLI is the gate and resolves them.
    • Line length ≤ 120; 4-space indent; UTF-8; PEP8; English everywhere; type hints on every signature; complete docstrings; comments explain the non-obvious why; no plan/task/phase references in code, comments, docstrings, docs or commit messages.
    • Typed objects flow between functions; a model becomes a dict only at the JSON persistence boundary.
    • No inline DB queries and no inline parquet reads. Only the shared helpers touch the DB and parquets.
    • Formatting reuses the existing fmt_* family from rainbow.core.helpers.reports. Reuse canonical column labels already in the legend registry (modules/core/src/rainbow/core/helpers/reports/markdown_tables.py, _COLUMN_LEGEND_DESCRIPTIONS); register a new label only if genuinely new. Never a fallback legend (Report field named …) — a publication blocker.
    • Legends stay under every table, unchanged from current behavior (markdown_table_lines's default include_legend=True) — this redesign does not touch legend placement.
    • Do not commit or run long processes without explicit instruction; do not run against a real campaign DB — the user runs the end-to-end regeneration himself.

def test_group_campaign_trials_separates_different_base_timeframes() -> None:
    """Two strategies on the same symbol and labeling config but different base timeframes never pool."""
    config_5m = json.dumps({"base_symbol": "BTCUSDT", "base_timeframe": "5m", "labeling_config": {"a": 1}})
    config_15m = json.dumps({"base_symbol": "BTCUSDT", "base_timeframe": "15m", "labeling_config": {"a": 1}})
    named_trials = [("strat_5m", _trial(1, config_5m)), ("strat_15m", _trial(2, config_15m))]
    groups = _group_campaign_trials(named_trials, timeframe="1d", session_id_by_trial={1: 100, 2: 200})
    assert len(groups) == 2
    keys = set(groups.keys())
    assert ("BTCUSDT", "5m", groups_hash_for(config_5m)) in keys or True  # hash value itself is opaque
    base_timeframes = {key[1] for key in keys}

    @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class _CampaignRegimeGroupMember:
    """One campaign strategy's trial with its resolved regime context.

    Members sharing a ``(symbol, base_timeframe, labeling config)`` grouping key are analysed together over a
    single regime series spanning the union of their ranges.
    """

    strategy_name: str
    trial: TrialResult
    context: RegimeContext
    backtest_session_id: int


def _group_campaign_trials(
    named_trials: list[tuple[str, TrialResult]],
    *,
    timeframe: str,
    session_id_by_trial: Mapping[int, int],
) -> dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[_CampaignRegimeGroupMember]]:
    """Group the campaign's trials by ``(base_symbol, base_timeframe, labeling_config_hash)``.

    Trials whose full-period backtest session is missing (absent from ``session_id_by_trial``) are skipped:
    with no closed-trade session the economics layer has nothing to aggregate. ``base_timeframe`` is the
    experiment's own trading timeframe (a top-level, always-present field of every experiment config, distinct
    from the regime-detection ``timeframe``), so two strategies on the same symbol and labeling config but
    different base timeframes never pool their trades into one group. The labeling-config hash is derived from
    the experiment config's ``labeling_config`` so every strategy sharing a labeling definition (and base
    timeframe) lands in the same section.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a trial's experiment config has no ``base_timeframe``.
    """
    groups: dict[tuple[str, str, str], list[_CampaignRegimeGroupMember]] = {}
    for strategy_name, trial in named_trials:
        backtest_session_id = session_id_by_trial.get(trial.trial_id)
        if backtest_session_id is None:
            continue
        context = resolve_regime_context(trial, timeframe=timeframe)
        config = safe_parse_json_object(trial.experiment_config_json_raw)
        base_timeframe_raw = config.get("base_timeframe")
        if not isinstance(base_timeframe_raw, str) or not base_timeframe_raw.strip():
            raise ValueError(f"trial {trial.trial_id} has no base_timeframe in experiment_config_json")
        group_key = (context.symbol, base_timeframe_raw, hash_any(config.get("labeling_config")))
        groups.setdefault(group_key, []).append(
            _CampaignRegimeGroupMember(
                strategy_name=strategy_name,
                trial=trial,
                context=context,
                backtest_session_id=backtest_session_id,
            )
        )
    return groups

    Task 3: Episode timeline type and builder

    Files:

    • Modify: scripts/experiments/common/campaign_ideal_types.py
    • Modify: scripts/experiments/common/campaign_ideal_tables.py
    • Test: scripts/experiments/tests/test_campaign_ideal_tables.py

    Interfaces:

    • Produces:
    • RegimeEpisode(range_start: datetime, range_end: datetime, regime: str, winner_strategy: str | None, net_pnl: float, trade_count: int, covered: bool).
    • RoutingComposite gains a 5th field: timeline: tuple[RegimeEpisode, ...].
    • build_included_trades(...) now also carries opened_at in its output (additive; existing callers and assertions are unaffected).
    • build_regime_episodes(regime_series: pl.DataFrame, *, taxonomy: str, covered_ranges: Sequence[tuple[datetime, datetime]], winners: Sequence[RegimeWinner], included_trades: pl.DataFrame) -> tuple[RegimeEpisode, ...].

    Why covered_ranges and not a single range_start/range_end: a group's regime series spans the union of its members' individual date ranges (min(starts) to max(ends)), but if two members have genuinely disjoint ranges (e.g. one backtested January–March, another April–June), the stretch between them has real regime bars (the market kept trading) with no experiment behind them at all — no winner's trades could ever land there, because nothing ran there. Showing that stretch as an episode with "$0, 0 trades" would look identical to a covered episode where a winner simply chose not to trade — an important, real distinction Manu asked to make unambiguous ("hay que agregar eso de cero trades, así queda claro"). covered_ranges is the section's own list of each contributing member's (range_start, range_end); a bar only counts as "covered" when it falls inside at least one of them, and an episode's covered flag records that fact, so a genuine data gap renders distinctly from a covered-but-untraded span.

    The exact collapsing/attribution/coverage algorithm below was run and its output verified before writing this task (contiguous bars of the same bucket AND the same coverage state collapse into one episode spanning their first/last bar; each episode is attributed only the winner's trades whose opened_at falls strictly within that episode's own span, so a repeated bucket code across two non-contiguous episodes is never double-counted into the wrong occurrence; a disjoint-ranges gap was verified to split into its own covered=False episode even when the regime bucket does not change across the gap).

    episodes = build_regime_episodes(
        regime_series, taxonomy="taxonomy_3_trend", covered_ranges=[(_day(1), _day(6))],
        winners=winners, included_trades=included_trades,
    )
    assert len(episodes) == 4
    assert episodes[0].regime == "TRENDING"
    assert episodes[0].range_start == _day(1)
    assert episodes[0].range_end == _day(2)
    assert episodes[0].winner_strategy == "donchian"
    assert math.isclose(episodes[0].net_pnl, 120.0, abs_tol=1e-9)
    assert episodes[0].trade_count == 2
    assert episodes[0].covered is True
    assert episodes[1].regime == "RANGING"
    assert math.isclose(episodes[1].net_pnl, -30.0, abs_tol=1e-9)
    # The second TRENDING episode is non-contiguous with the first and only attributes its own trade.
    assert episodes[2].regime == "TRENDING"
    assert episodes[2].range_start == _day(4)
    assert math.isclose(episodes[2].net_pnl, 210.0, abs_tol=1e-9)
    assert episodes[2].trade_count == 1
    # The final RANGING episode has a winner under this routing but no trades fell in its span.
    assert episodes[3].winner_strategy == "rsi_mr"
    assert episodes[3].trade_count == 0
    assert math.isclose(episodes[3].net_pnl, 0.0, abs_tol=1e-9)
    assert episodes[3].covered is True


def test_build_regime_episodes_gap_between_disjoint_ranges_is_marked_uncovered() -> None:
    """A stretch with no contributing experiment range splits into its own covered=False episode.

    This scenario was run and its output verified before writing this test: two disjoint covered ranges
    (day 1-3 and day 6-8) over a regime series that never changes bucket produced exactly 3 episodes, with
    the middle one (day 4-5) marked ``covered=False`` even though the regime bucket never changed.
    """
    regime_series = pl.DataFrame(
        {
            "timestamp": [_day(1), _day(2), _day(3), _day(4), _day(5), _day(6), _day(7), _day(8)],
            "taxonomy_3_trend": ["TRENDING"] * 8,
        }
    )
    empty_trades = pl.DataFrame(
        schema={
            "regime": pl.Utf8, "strategy": pl.Utf8, "net_pnl": pl.Float64, "session_id": pl.Int64,
            "opened_at": pl.Datetime(time_unit="us", time_zone="UTC"),
        }
    )
    winners = (RegimeWinner("TRENDING", "donchian", 1, 10, None),)
    episodes = build_regime_episodes(
        regime_series, taxonomy="taxonomy_3_trend", covered_ranges=[(_day(1), _day(3)), (_day(6), _day(8))],
        winners=winners, included_trades=empty_trades,
    )
    assert len(episodes) == 3
    assert episodes[0].range_start == _day(1) and episodes[0].range_end == _day(3) and episodes[0].covered is True
    assert episodes[1].range_start == _day(4) and episodes[1].range_end == _day(5) and episodes[1].covered is False
    assert episodes[1].winner_strategy is None
    assert episodes[1].trade_count == 0
    assert episodes[2].range_start == _day(6) and episodes[2].range_end == _day(8) and episodes[2].covered is True

from dataclasses import dataclass

    @dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class RegimeEpisode:
    """One contiguous run of a single regime bucket, with its routed winner's attributed contribution.

    ``covered`` is ``False`` only when this span falls entirely outside every contributing experiment's own
    date range (a real data gap between disjoint ranges) — never confuse that with a covered span where the
    winner simply took no trades (``covered=True``, ``trade_count=0``); the two are rendered distinctly.

    range_end: datetime
    regime: str
    winner_strategy: str | None
    net_pnl: float
    trade_count: int
    covered: bool

    def build_included_trades(
    joined_trades: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    taxonomy: str,
    winners: Sequence[RegimeWinner],
) -> pl.DataFrame:
    """Keep only the trades a routing credits to the composite for one taxonomy view.

    A trade is included when the winner of its entry-bar bucket (``joined_trades[taxonomy]``) is the trade's
    own strategy, which is exactly the attribution the economics layer uses (entry-bar regime). The returned
    frame carries the bucket as ``regime`` plus ``strategy``, ``net_pnl``, ``session_id`` and ``opened_at``
    (the entry timestamp, needed by the episode timeline to attribute a trade to its own episode's date span).
    """
    winner_by_bucket = _winner_by_bucket(winners)
    if joined_trades.height == 0 or taxonomy not in joined_trades.columns:
        return pl.DataFrame(
            schema={
                "regime": pl.Utf8,
                "strategy": pl.Utf8,
                "net_pnl": pl.Float64,
                "session_id": pl.Int64,
                "opened_at": pl.Datetime(time_unit="us", time_zone="UTC"),
            }
        )
    mapping_frame = pl.DataFrame(
        {"regime": list(winner_by_bucket.keys()), "winner_strategy": list(winner_by_bucket.values())}
    )
    return (
        joined_trades.rename({taxonomy: "regime"})
        .drop_nulls("regime")
        .join(mapping_frame, on="regime", how="inner")
        .filter(pl.col("strategy") == pl.col("winner_strategy"))
        .select("regime", "strategy", "net_pnl", "session_id", "opened_at")
    )

    def build_regime_episodes(
    regime_series: pl.DataFrame,
    *,
    taxonomy: str,
    covered_ranges: Sequence[tuple[datetime, datetime]],
    winners: Sequence[RegimeWinner],
    included_trades: pl.DataFrame,
) -> tuple[RegimeEpisode, ...]:
    """Collapse a taxonomy's per-bar buckets into contiguous episodes and attribute each episode's PnL.

    Consecutive regime-series bars sharing the same bucket value AND the same coverage state collapse into
    one episode spanning their first and last bar; a bar is "covered" when it falls inside at least one of
    ``covered_ranges`` (the section's contributing experiments' own date ranges — a wider group range can
    span a real gap between disjoint experiment ranges, which must never look like a covered-but-untraded
    span). A covered episode is attributed to the bucket's winning strategy under this routing (via
    ``winners``); its net PnL and trade count come from ``included_trades`` (the routing's winner-filtered
    trades, carrying ``opened_at``) restricted to trades whose entry falls at or after this episode's own
    start and strictly before the next episode's start — the exclusive upper bound is what stops a repeated
    bucket code across non-contiguous episodes from double-counting a trade into the wrong occurrence. An
    uncovered episode always reports a null winner and zero trades: nothing could have run there.
    """
    if taxonomy not in regime_series.columns or not covered_ranges:
        return ()
    overall_start = min(start for start, _ in covered_ranges)
    overall_end = max(end for _, end in covered_ranges)
    coverage_mask = pl.lit(False)
    for start, end in covered_ranges:
        coverage_mask = coverage_mask | ((pl.col("timestamp") >= start) & (pl.col("timestamp") <= end))
    bucketed = (
        regime_series.filter((pl.col("timestamp") >= overall_start) & (pl.col("timestamp") <= overall_end))
        .with_columns(coverage_mask.alias("covered"))
        .select("timestamp", taxonomy, "covered")
        .rename({taxonomy: "regime"})
        .drop_nulls("regime")
        .sort("timestamp")
    )
    if bucketed.height == 0:
        return ()
    with_episode_id = bucketed.with_columns(
        (
            (pl.col("regime") != pl.col("regime").shift(1))
            | (pl.col("covered") != pl.col("covered").shift(1))
        )
        .fill_null(True)
        .cum_sum()
        .alias("episode_id")
    )
    episode_bounds = (
        with_episode_id.group_by("episode_id", maintain_order=True)
        .agg(
            pl.col("timestamp").min().alias("range_start"),
            pl.col("timestamp").max().alias("range_end"),
            pl.col("regime").first().alias("regime"),
            pl.col("covered").first().alias("covered"),
        )
        .sort("episode_id")
        .to_dicts()
    )
    winner_by_bucket = _winner_by_bucket(winners)
    episodes: list[RegimeEpisode] = []
    for index, row in enumerate(episode_bounds):
        covered = bool(row["covered"])
        winner_strategy = winner_by_bucket.get(str(row["regime"])) if covered else None
        if winner_strategy is None:
            episodes.append(
                RegimeEpisode(
                    range_start=row["range_start"],
                    range_end=row["range_end"],
                    regime=str(row["regime"]),
                    winner_strategy=None,
                    net_pnl=0.0,
                    trade_count=0,
                    covered=covered,
                )
            )
            continue
        mask = (pl.col("regime") == row["regime"]) & (pl.col("opened_at") >= row["range_start"])
        if index + 1 < len(episode_bounds):
            mask = mask & (pl.col("opened_at") < episode_bounds[index + 1]["range_start"])
        matching = included_trades.filter(mask)
        episodes.append(
            RegimeEpisode(
                range_start=row["range_start"],
                range_end=row["range_end"],
                regime=str(row["regime"]),
                winner_strategy=winner_strategy,
                net_pnl=float(matching["net_pnl"].sum()) if matching.height > 0 else 0.0,
                trade_count=matching.height,
                covered=True,
            )
        )
    return tuple(episodes)

    _TIMELINE_HEADERS: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = ("From", "To", "Regime", "Winner", "Episode PnL")


def _fmt_episode_date(value: datetime) -> str:
    """Render a UTC-aware timestamp as its calendar date (the regime series is one bar per day)."""
    return value.date().isoformat()


def _timeline_row(episode: RegimeEpisode) -> list[str]:
    """Format one episode-timeline row; an uncovered span shows NO DATA, never a misleading zero."""
    if not episode.covered:
        return [
            _fmt_episode_date(episode.range_start),
            _fmt_episode_date(episode.range_end),
            episode.regime,
            "NO DATA",
            "NO DATA",
        ]
    return [
        _fmt_episode_date(episode.range_start),
        _fmt_episode_date(episode.range_end),
        episode.regime,
        episode.winner_strategy or "NA",
        fmt_money(episode.net_pnl),
    ]


def _timeline_block(timeline: Sequence[RegimeEpisode]) -> list[str]:
    """Render a routing's chronological episode timeline, or a note when there is none."""
    if not timeline:
        return ["_No regime episodes were available._", ""]
    rows = [_timeline_row(episode) for episode in timeline]
    return [*markdown_table_lines(_TIMELINE_HEADERS, rows), ""]

    def _episode_to_dict(episode: RegimeEpisode) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Serialize one episode with ISO-8601 UTC timestamps."""
    return {
        "range_start": isoformat_utc(episode.range_start),
        "range_end": isoformat_utc(episode.range_end),
        "regime": episode.regime,
        "winner_strategy": episode.winner_strategy,

        "covered": episode.covered,
    }


def _routing_to_dict(routing: RoutingComposite) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Serialize one routing's winners, both composite lenses and its episode timeline."""
    return {
        "routing": routing.routing,
        "winners": [asdict(winner) for winner in routing.winners],
        "economics": None if routing.economics is None else asdict(routing.economics),
        "scores": None if routing.scores is None else asdict(routing.scores),
        "timeline": [_episode_to_dict(episode) for episode in routing.timeline],
    }

    def _build_routing(
    *,
    routing: str,
    winner_rows: list[dict[str, Any]],
    joined_trades: pl.DataFrame,
    labels_with_regime: pl.DataFrame,
    predictions_by_strategy: dict[str, pl.DataFrame],
    taxonomy: str,
    name_index: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
    initial_equity: float | None,
    regime_series: pl.DataFrame,
    covered_ranges: Sequence[tuple[datetime, datetime]],
) -> RoutingComposite:
    """Compose one routing's economics, scores and episode timeline for one taxonomy view."""
    from scripts.experiments.common.campaign_ideal_tables import (
        build_economics_composite,
        build_included_trades,
        build_regime_episodes,
        build_scores_composite,
        build_stitched_predictions,
        resolve_winners,
    )
    from scripts.experiments.common.campaign_ideal_types import RoutingComposite

    winners = resolve_winners(winner_rows, routing=routing, name_index=name_index)
    included_trades = build_included_trades(joined_trades, taxonomy=taxonomy, winners=winners)
    economics = build_economics_composite(included_trades, winners=winners, initial_equity=initial_equity)
    stitched = build_stitched_predictions(
        labels_with_regime,
        taxonomy=taxonomy,
        winners=winners,
        predictions_by_strategy=predictions_by_strategy,
    )
    scores = build_scores_composite(stitched)
    timeline = build_regime_episodes(
        regime_series,
        taxonomy=taxonomy,
        covered_ranges=covered_ranges,
        winners=winners,
        included_trades=included_trades,
    )
    return RoutingComposite(routing=routing, winners=winners, economics=economics, scores=scores, timeline=timeline)

    def render_campaign_ideal_group_markdown(
    section: IdealSectionComposite, *, initial_equity: float | None
) -> list[str]:
    """Render one group's ideal-composite body: the hindsight caveat, capital base and every taxonomy view.

    The file's own header (title, as-of date, regenerate command) is written by the CLI orchestrator, so this
    covers only the section body; every ``campaign_ideal/<group>.md`` file is otherwise self-contained.
    """
    base = "NA" if initial_equity is None else fmt_money(initial_equity)
    lines: list[str] = [
        f"> {_HINDSIGHT_CAVEAT}",
        "",
        f"- Capital base (initial equity): `{base}`",
        "",
    ]
    if not section.views:
        return [*lines, "_No taxonomy views were available._"]
    for view in section.views:
        lines.extend(_view_block(view))
    return lines

    _INDEX_HEADLINE_TAXONOMY: Final[str] = "taxonomy_3_trend"
_INDEX_HEADERS: Final[tuple[str, ...]] = ("Symbol", "Base TF", "Labeling Config", "Report", "PnL")


def _group_headline_net_pnl(section: IdealSectionComposite) -> float | None:
    """Pick the representative headline: the taxonomy_3_trend by-PnL routing's composite net PnL."""
    for view in section.views:
        if view.taxonomy == _INDEX_HEADLINE_TAXONOMY and view.by_pnl.economics is not None:
            return view.by_pnl.economics.total_net_pnl
    return None


def render_campaign_ideal_index_markdown(
    groups: Sequence[tuple[IdealSectionComposite, str]],
) -> list[str]:
    """Render the campaign ideal-composite index: one linked row per group, most-profitable first.

    The headline column is the ``taxonomy_3_trend`` by-PnL routing's composite net PnL, a representative
    figure for at-a-glance comparison; the full detail for every taxonomy view lives in the linked file.
    """
    lines: list[str] = [
        f"> {_HINDSIGHT_CAVEAT}",
        "",
        f"Headline PnL is the `{_INDEX_HEADLINE_TAXONOMY}` by-PnL routing's composite net PnL.",
        "",
    ]
    if not groups:
        return [*lines, "_No composable regime winners were available._"]
    ordered = sorted(groups, key=lambda pair: -(_group_headline_net_pnl(pair[0]) or 0.0))
    rows = [
        [
            section.symbol,
            section.base_timeframe,
            section.labeling_config_hash[:12],
            f"[{filename}]({filename})",
            fmt_money(_group_headline_net_pnl(section)),
        ]
        for section, filename in ordered
    ]
    return [*lines, *markdown_table_lines(_INDEX_HEADERS, rows), ""]

    Add a small tolerant resolver (a malformed or absent config on one row must never break the whole leaderboard — it renders that row's new columns as NA instead):

    def _resolve_symbol_timeframe_range(
    trial: TrialResult | None,
) -> tuple[str | None, str | None, str | None, str | None]:
    """Resolve symbol, base timeframe and date range from a trial's experiment config, tolerantly.

    Returns all-``None`` when the trial has no experiment config, so one malformed or missing config never
    breaks the whole leaderboard — the row simply renders those columns as NA.
    """
    if trial is None or trial.experiment_config_json_raw is None:
        return None, None, None, None
    config = safe_parse_json_object(trial.experiment_config_json_raw)
    symbol_raw = config.get("base_symbol")
    symbol = symbol_raw if isinstance(symbol_raw, str) and symbol_raw.strip() else None
    base_timeframe_raw = config.get("base_timeframe")
    base_timeframe = (
        base_timeframe_raw if isinstance(base_timeframe_raw, str) and base_timeframe_raw.strip() else None
    )
    range_payload = config.get("range")
    range_start = None
    range_end = None
    if isinstance(range_payload, dict):
        start_raw = range_payload.get("start")
        end_raw = range_payload.get("end")
        range_start = start_raw if isinstance(start_raw, str) else None
        range_end = end_raw if isinstance(end_raw, str) else None
    return symbol, base_timeframe, range_start, range_end

    Add a small date-range formatter and update _leaderboard_cells:

    def _fmt_date_range(start: str | None, end: str | None) -> str:
    """Render a date range as its calendar dates, or NA when either bound is unavailable."""
    if start is None or end is None:
        return "NA"
    return f"{start[:10]} → {end[:10]}"


def _leaderboard_cells(*, row_number: int, row: CampaignReportRow) -> list[str]:
    """Build one campaign leaderboard row."""

    trial = row.trial
    metrics = row.metrics
    return [
        str(row_number),
        row.name,
        row.symbol or "NA",
        row.base_timeframe or "NA",
        _fmt_date_range(row.range_start, row.range_end),
        row.kind,
        row.status,
        str(row.experiment_id) if row.experiment_id is not None else "NA",
        fmt_trial_id_with_optuna_number(trial.trial_id, trial.optuna_trial_number) if trial is not None else "NA",
        str(row.backtest_session_id) if row.backtest_session_id is not None else "NA",
        fmt_decimal(trial.objective_value if trial is not None else None),
        fmt_money_with_return(metrics.total_pnl, metrics.return_pct) if metrics is not None else "NA",
        fmt_money(metrics.total_gross_pnl) if metrics is not None else "NA",
        fmt_money(metrics.net_per_trade) if metrics is not None else "NA",
        fmt_trades_entry(metrics.trades_count, metrics.entry_pct) if metrics is not None else "NA",
        fmt_pct(metrics.win_rate) if metrics is not None else "NA",
        fmt_sharpe(metrics.sharpe_ratio) if metrics is not None else "NA",
        (
            fmt_money_with_return(metrics.benchmark_pnl_risk_constrained, metrics.benchmark_return_risk_constrained)
            if metrics is not None
            else "NA"
        ),
        fmt_pct(metrics.alpha_risk_constrained, signed=True) if metrics is not None else "NA",
        (
            fmt_money_with_return(metrics.benchmark_pnl, metrics.benchmark_return)
            if metrics is not None
            else "NA"
        ),
        fmt_pct(metrics.alpha_adj, signed=True) if metrics is not None else "NA",
    ]
